guide.summary: GitLab documents OAuth 2.0 applications that let third-party services access GitLab resources for a user. Register a user-owned application, obtain user consent through the authorization-code flow, and request the read_api scope, which covers read access to projects through the API. Test with a representative account, then call the documented project issues list endpoint with GET only, following cursor pagination. Confirm the connected person's project role allows viewing issues. Customer-wide distribution and review requirements are not documented in the supplied sources and remain unknown.

findings.title: OAuth applications are documented for third-party access on behalf of a user
findings.detail: GitLab's OAuth 2.0 identity provider API lets third-party services access resources for a user. Applications are registered in the user's account settings.

evidence.quote: Use this API to allow third-party services to access GitLab resources for a user
registered first via the /user_settings/applications page in your user’s account.

findings.title: Request read_api to read issues in projects through the API
findings.detail: read_api grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects. It is the documented read-only scope that covers listing project issues. Do not request read_user, which covers only the profile and user endpoints.
findings.appliesWhen: Reading issue titles through the project issues list endpoint

evidence.quote: read_api Grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects, the container registry, and the package registry.
Lists all issues for a specified project.

findings.title: Connected person must have access to the project's issues
findings.detail: Private projects require credentials, and the connected user's role in the project determines visibility. The issue list returns only what that user can see.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer account connects and reads a private project

evidence.quote: If the project is private, you need to provide credentials to authorize.
Roles define a user’s permissions in a group or project.

findings.title: Access tokens can have configurable expiry
findings.detail: OAuth access token expiry is configurable by instance administrators. The integration should handle re-authorization when a token expires.
findings.appliesWhen: The instance applies a token expiry setting

evidence.quote: Access token expiration History OAuth access token expiry configurable by instance administrators introduced in GitLab 19.1.

steps.title: Read issue titles from a project using pagination
steps.detail: Call the project issues list with the OAuth token and read titles from the first page. The documented route is /projects/:id/issues under the /api/v4 base path. Use the documented cursor parameter to request the next page. Expected response: a JSON array of issues, each with a title. Boundary check: confirm the token scope is read_api and the request log contains only GET calls to the issues endpoint.
steps.doneWhen: Titles from at least two pages are read and the request log shows only GET requests.

steps.detail: Inspect the token details through the documented token info endpoint. Confirm the scope is read_api and no issue was created, updated, or deleted during testing. Do not send write requests to test this boundary.
steps.doneWhen: Token info shows read_api and the project's issue list is unchanged after testing.
